items.title: Agriculture in the Economy & Cropping Seasons
items.body:
## Place in the economy

- Agriculture and allied sectors contribute about **18% of GVA/GDP** but engage roughly **45-46% of the workforce**, with **over 58% of rural households** dependent on it — a sign of **low relative productivity and disguised unemployment**.
- Its GDP share has **declined** over time (structural shift agriculture → services), even as absolute output rose.
- About **52% of cultivated land is rainfed**, so output is highly monsoon-sensitive.

## Cropping seasons

| Season | Sowing | Harvest | Major crops |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kharif** | Jun-Jul (monsoon) | Sep-Oct | Rice, maize, cotton, bajra, jowar, groundnut, soybean |
| **Rabi** | Oct-Dec (winter) | Mar-May | Wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas |
| **Zaid** | Mar-Jun (summer) | Jun-Aug | Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, fodder |

- Kharif needs high temperature + rainfall; Rabi needs cool growth + warm ripening; Zaid are short-duration crops needing assured irrigation.
keyPoints: Agriculture is ~18% of GVA but employs ~45-46% of the workforce; >58% of rural households depend on it.
Agriculture's GDP share has fallen over time as services grew (structural transformation).
About 52% of India's cultivable land is rainfed, making output monsoon-dependent.
Kharif = monsoon crops (rice, cotton) sown Jun-Jul; Rabi = winter crops (wheat, gram) sown Oct-Dec; Zaid = short summer crops (watermelon).
items.mnemonic: Seasons by weather: Kharif = rains, Rabi = winter, Zaid = summer.

items.title: Green Revolution & Coloured Revolutions
items.body:
## Green Revolution

- Introduced **post-1965** to raise foodgrain output and secure food self-sufficiency, using **HYV seeds + chemical fertilisers + assured irrigation + double-cropping**.
- **M.S. Swaminathan** is its Indian father, building on **Norman Borlaug's** HYV wheat; early gains concentrated in **wheat and rice** in **Punjab, Haryana and western UP**.
- Made India self-sufficient in foodgrains, but caused **soil-nutrient and groundwater depletion, higher input costs, chemical overuse and regional imbalance**.
- **Evergreen Revolution** (Swaminathan) stresses sustainable, ecology-friendly productivity.

## Coloured revolutions

| Revolution | Product |
|---|---|
| Green | Foodgrains (wheat, rice) |
| White (Operation Flood) | Milk |
| Blue | Fisheries |
| Yellow | Oilseeds/edible oil |
| Pink | Meat/prawn |
| Golden | Horticulture/honey |
| Silver | Eggs/poultry |
| Golden Fibre | Jute |
keyPoints: Green Revolution (post-1965) used HYV seeds, fertiliser and irrigation; M.S. Swaminathan (with Borlaug's work) led it in India.
Early Green Revolution gains were in wheat/rice in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.
Drawbacks: groundwater and soil depletion, higher costs, regional imbalance.
White = milk (Operation Flood, Kurien); Blue = fish; Yellow = oilseeds; Pink = meat/prawn; Golden = honey/horticulture.
items.mnemonic: Milk is White, water is Blue, oil is Yellow — colour matches the product.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Agriculture (Green Revolution; Revolutions)

items.title: Land Reforms & Holding Categories
items.body:
## Post-Independence land reforms

- **Abolition of intermediaries** — zamindari abolished, ownership/occupancy given to actual cultivators.
- **Tenancy reforms** — state laws to protect tenant rights and regulate rent.
- **Land ceilings** — caps on holdings to check concentration (surplus redistributed).
- **Consolidation of holdings** — merging scattered plots to cut fragmentation.
- **Cooperative farming** and the **Bhoodan Movement** (1951, **Acharya Vinoba Bhave**; first donation by **V. Ramachandra Reddy**) for voluntary land gifts.
- **Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016** (NITI Aayog) legalises leasing and gives lessees institutional-credit access.

## Holding categories

| Size | Class |
|---|---|
| <1 ha | Marginal |
| 1-2 ha | Small |
| 2-4 ha | Semi-medium |
| 4-10 ha | Medium |
| >10 ha | Large |

- Marginal + small holdings dominate (over 85% of all holdings), keeping average farm size tiny.
keyPoints: Land reforms had four planks: abolition of intermediaries, tenancy regulation, land ceilings, consolidation (plus cooperative farming).
Bhoodan Movement (1951) led by Acharya Vinoba Bhave; first land donation by V. Ramachandra Reddy.
Land classes: <1 ha marginal, 1-2 ha small, 2-4 ha semi-medium, 4-10 ha medium, >10 ha large.
Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 (NITI Aayog) legitimises leasing and tenant credit access.

items.title: MSP, CACP & Cost Concepts
items.body:
## Minimum Support Price

- **MSP** is a pre-announced floor price protecting farmers from sharp price falls; introduced in **1965-66** (first announced for **wheat, 1966-67**) with the Green Revolution.
- Recommended by the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)** — set up in **1965 as the Agricultural Prices Commission (APC), renamed CACP in 1985** — and approved by the **Cabinet (CCEA)**; announced for **23 crops** (including **niger**, a Kharif oilseed).
- **Sugarcane** instead gets a **Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP)**, approved by the **CCEA** (CACP only recommends); States may add a higher **State Advised Price (SAP)**.
- Farm produce is marketed under the **APMC Act enacted by each State**; **e-NAM (2016)** is the pan-India electronic mandi platform.

## The 23 crops

- **7 cereals** (paddy, wheat, barley, jowar, bajra, maize, ragi), **5 pulses** (gram, arhar, moong, urad, lentil), **7 oilseeds**, **4 commercial** (cotton, sugarcane [FRP], raw jute, copra).

## Cost concepts

| Cost | Includes |
|---|---|
| **A2** | Paid-out costs (seeds, fertiliser, irrigation, hired labour) |
| **A2+FL** | A2 + imputed family labour |
| **C2** | A2+FL + imputed rent & interest on owned land/capital |

- **Swaminathan Commission** urged MSP = **C2 + 50%**; the government uses **A2+FL+50%**.
- Procured by **FCI** (foodgrains), **NAFED** (pulses/oilseeds), **CCI** (cotton).
- **Challenges**: procurement skewed to Punjab/Haryana/MP, low awareness (~23%), narrow crop coverage, water-intensive-crop bias, fiscal burden.
keyPoints: MSP introduced 1965-66; recommended by CACP, announced for 23 crops (7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 4 commercial).
MSP first announced for wheat (1966-67); CACP began as the Agricultural Prices Commission (APC) in 1965, renamed CACP in 1985.
Sugarcane gets a Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) approved by the CCEA (CACP recommends); States may add a State Advised Price (SAP).
Farm produce is regulated under State-enacted APMC Acts; e-NAM (2016) is the pan-India electronic mandi platform; niger is a Kharif oilseed under MSP.
A2 = paid-out costs; A2+FL adds family labour; C2 adds imputed rent/interest on owned assets.
Swaminathan Commission recommended MSP = C2 + 50%; government uses A2+FL+50%.
Procurement: FCI (foodgrains), NAFED (pulses/oilseeds), CCI (cotton); common paddy MSP 2025-26 = ₹2,369/quintal.
MSP is criticised for regional skew, low awareness and encouraging water-guzzling paddy/wheat.
items.mnemonic: Cost ladder A2 → A2+FL → C2 = paid → +family labour → +owned-asset rent/interest.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Agriculture (MSP; costs); Swaminathan Commission; CACP 2025-26

items.title: Farmer-Welfare Schemes & Institutional Credit
items.body:
## Key schemes

| Scheme | Year | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| **PM-KISAN** | 2018/19 | ₹6,000/year income support (3 × ₹2,000, DBT); 20th instalment Aug 2025 |
| **PMFBY** | 2016 | Crop insurance; farmer premium 2% Kharif / 1.5% Rabi / 5% commercial; voluntary since 2020 |
| **PM Kisan Maan Dhan** | 2019 | ₹3,000/month pension for small farmers after 60 |
| **Soil Health Card** | 2015 | Nutrient-status advisory |
| **PMKSY** | 2015 | Irrigation potential & 'per drop more crop' |
| **KUSUM** | 2019 | Solar-powered irrigation pumps |
| **e-NAM** | 2016 | Online national agri-market linking mandis |

## Institutional credit

- **NABARD** (1982) is the apex refinancing body for rural/agri credit.
- Channels: **commercial banks, cooperatives, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**.
- **Kisan Credit Card (KCC, 1998)** gives short-term crop-loan access; agriculture is a **priority-sector lending** target.
keyPoints: PM-KISAN (2018/19): ₹6,000/year in 3 instalments via DBT; 20th instalment released Aug 2025.
PMFBY (2016): crop insurance, premiums 2%/1.5%/5%, voluntary for loanee farmers since 2020.
KUSUM = solar pumps; Soil Health Card = nutrient advisory; PMKSY = irrigation; e-NAM = online mandi market.
NABARD (1982) is the apex rural-credit refinancer; KCC (1998) gives farmers short-term crop loans.
Institutional credit flows via commercial banks, cooperatives and RRBs under priority-sector lending.

items.title: Food Security, NFSA & the Andhra Pradesh Angle
items.body:
## Food security

- FAO's **four dimensions**: **Availability, Accessibility, Utilization, Stability**.
- **NFSA 2013**: **5 kg/person/month** for priority households, **35 kg/household** for **Antyodaya (AAY)**; covers **75% rural + 50% urban (~67%, ~813 million)**. The **eldest woman aged ≥18 is the head of the household** for the ration card; **pregnant & lactating women** get maternity benefit and take-home rations (~**1600 kcal/day**).
- Delivery via **PDS/TPDS**; **One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)** makes cards portable for migrants; **PMGKAY** provides free foodgrains (free since Jan 2023).
- Buffer stocks and procurement run through the **FCI**.
- Challenges: ~195 million undernourished, high stunting/anaemia, PDS leakages, post-harvest losses.

## Andhra Pradesh angle

- **Rice** is the staple, irrigated by the **Krishna, Godavari, Penna and Tungabhadra** — the Krishna-Godavari delta is a **'rice bowl'**.
- AP is India's **largest shrimp producer (~70%)** and a leading marine-exporter (Vannamei shrimp); second-longest coastline.
- **Horticulture leader**: **1st in chillies, cocoa, lime, oil palm, papaya and tomato**; 2nd in cashew, mango and sweet orange.
- Agriculture engages about **60% of AP's people**. AP runs **Annadata Sukhibhava** — a **farmer income-support** scheme topping up PM-KISAN (**₹6,600 cr in Budget 2026-27**) — delivered through village-level single-window **Rythu Bharosa Kendras (RBKs)**.
- **Major irrigation projects:** **Polavaram** (national multipurpose project on the **Godavari**, targeted before the **Godavari Pushkarams 2027**), **Handri-Neeva**, **Galeru-Nagari**, **Veligonda** and **Pattiseema** (Godavari→Krishna lift). AP's diversified push is called the **Rainbow Revolution** (holistic/integrated agriculture).
- **India** is the **world's largest exporter of rice** and ranks **#1 or #2 globally** in rice, wheat, milk, pulses, sugarcane, cotton and spices production.
keyPoints: FAO food-security dimensions: Availability, Accessibility, Utilization, Stability.
NFSA 2013: 5 kg/person/month (priority), 35 kg/household (AAY); ~67% of population (~813 million); eldest woman ≥18 = head of household for the ration card.
ONORC makes ration cards portable; PMGKAY gives free foodgrains via FCI buffer stocks.
AP is India's largest shrimp producer (~70%) with the second-longest coastline; India is the world's largest rice exporter.
AP ranks 1st in chillies, cocoa, lime, oil palm, papaya and tomato; rice bowl in the Krishna-Godavari delta.

AP farmer welfare: Annadata Sukhibhava (₹6,600 cr, Budget 2026-27) via Rythu Bharosa Kendras; key projects Polavaram (before 2027 Pushkarams), Handri-Neeva, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Pattiseema; 'Rainbow Revolution'.
